elements.evidence: The added paragraph expressly permits Company to terminate the Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its termination-for-convenience right on thirty (30) days' notice.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph requires thirty (30) days' advance notice.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph expressly requires advance written notice to Contractor.

elements.element: Upon Customer's termination for convenience, Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees attributable to the period after termination.
elements.evidence: Contractor must refund Company, pro rata, any prepaid fees for the period after the effective termination date.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section (a) permits Contractor to terminate for convenience only when there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, so Contractor cannot terminate for convenience during an active Statement of Work.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60–90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The added right uses thirty (30) days' notice, which is outside the specified 60–90-day fallback range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed; therefore, no fee exceeds the three-month cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section (a) allows Contractor to terminate whenever no uncompleted Statement of Work is outstanding, rather than expressly limiting termination to the end of a term.

elements.element: Vendor's termination for convenience requires ninety (90) days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section (a) permits Contractor to terminate on only fifteen (15) days' advance notice.

result.reason: The redline satisfies every preferred requirement: Company receives an unrestricted convenience-termination right covering the Agreement and Statements of Work on 30 days' written notice, with the required pro-rata refund, while Contractor remains unable to terminate during an active Statement of Work. The existing cause-based termination, accrued-payment, and work-in-progress provisions remain intact. The fallback is not independently satisfied because the Customer notice period is 30 rather than 60–90 days, and Contractor retains a 15-day convenience right whenever no Statement of Work is outstanding rather than a 90-day right exercisable only at term-end.
